recognize_zh: 低倍骨髓抹片中散布大量中大型、細胞質少、染色質細緻的芽細胞（blasts）小叢集，成熟中的顆粒球與紅血球前驅細胞相對稀少；這種外觀只提示急性骨髓性白血病，CEBPA 突變須靠分子檢驗確認。
features: Numerous medium-to-large blasts scattered singly and in small clusters
High N:C ratio with round to slightly irregular nuclei and fine chromatin
Scant pale basophilic cytoplasm; granules and Auer rods not resolvable at this low magnification
Relative paucity of maturing granulocytes and erythroid precursors
Blood-rich smear with fat-droplet spaces in the background
describe_en: Low-power view of a bone marrow aspirate smear shows a hemodilute background with fat spaces and a markedly increased population of medium-to-large blasts occurring singly and in loose clusters. The blasts have high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, fine chromatin and scant basophilic cytoplasm; cytoplasmic granules and Auer rods cannot be evaluated at this magnification. Maturing myeloid and erythroid elements are sparse. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia; the CEBPA mutation status is a molecular finding and cannot be inferred from morphology.

ddx.vs: Often shows cup-like nuclear invaginations and monocytic differentiation, but separation from CEBPA-mutated AML requires molecular testing.
Lymphoblasts are MPO-negative and express lymphoid markers (CD19/CD79a or cCD3) on flow cytometry, whereas CEBPA-mutated AML blasts are typically MPO-positive with CD34/CD13/CD33 and aberrant CD7.
Requires multilineage dysplasia or MDS-defining cytogenetics/mutations, which are not evaluable in this low-power field.
